evals.prompt: I have a .NET Lambda using MinimalLambda. Create a clean Program.cs for an order processor with DI, an inline MapHandler arrow function, cancellation token propagation, and a service boundary for non-Lambda business logic. Also mention what package/usings I need.
evals.expected_output: Uses LambdaApplication.CreateBuilder, registers services before Build, maps exactly one inline handler with one [FromEvent] OrderRequest parameter, injects IOrderService and CancellationToken, delegates business logic to the service, calls RunAsync, and explains MinimalLambda package/usings.

assertions.text: Output uses inline MapHandler arrow function as the Lambda adapter and delegates non-trivial business logic to a service.
Handler signature has exactly one [FromEvent] payload parameter and propagates CancellationToken.
Output does not recommend manual JSON parsing or reflection-based dispatch.

evals.prompt: We're building an API Gateway HTTP API v2 Lambda with MinimalLambda and Native AOT. Show the request/response envelope pattern and serializer setup for CreateOrderRequest/CreateOrderResponse.
evals.expected_output: Selects MinimalLambda.Envelopes.ApiGateway, uses ApiGatewayV2RequestEnvelope<T> and ApiGatewayV2ResponseEnvelope<T> or ApiGatewayV2Result, includes JsonSerializerContext entries for envelope and payload/response, registers AddLambdaSerializerWithContext and ConfigureEnvelopeOptions.

assertions.text: Output chooses API Gateway v2 envelope/result types, not v1-only types.
Output configures envelope options TypeInfoResolver for nested body content.
Output includes both envelope and payload/response types in JsonSerializerContext.

evals.prompt: My MinimalLambda middleware isn't seeing the order request and sometimes scoped data leaks between invocations. Review likely causes and show a better inline middleware pattern, noting when to extract a class or delegate to a service.
evals.expected_output: Explains middleware order before MapHandler, uses ILambdaInvocationContext feature helpers like TryGetEvent/GetResponse, distinguishes Items vs Properties, warns against singleton/scoped leaks, shows thin inline middleware, says to extract class middleware or services only when logic is complex/reusable/stateful/test-worthy, and keeps Lambda context objects out of services.

assertions.text: Output says middleware should be registered before MapHandler.
Output uses context.TryGetEvent<T>() or features for typed event access.
Output distinguishes per-invocation Items from cross-invocation Properties/singletons.
Output warns against capturing scoped services/state in singletons.
Output prefers inline middleware for simple Lambda glue and extracts class middleware/services only for complex, reusable, stateful, or separately tested logic.
Output says inline middleware does not support direct service injection and uses context.ServiceProvider, class middleware, or factory middleware for dependencies.
Output does not pass ILambdaInvocationContext, ILambdaContext, or feature collections into application services; it extracts needed domain values at the edge.

evals.prompt: Add integration tests for a MinimalLambda function. I need to override IOrderService in tests, invoke a typed event, assert success, and know when not to use a shared fixture.
evals.expected_output: Uses MinimalLambda.Testing LambdaApplicationFactory<Program>, WithHostBuilder ConfigureServices override, InvokeAsync<TEvent,TResponse>, WasSuccess assertion, and warns shared factory reuses OnInit/singletons.

assertions.text: Output invokes typed event using InvokeAsync<TEvent,TResponse>().
Output warns shared fixtures reuse OnInit and singleton state.
